problem: writeExportFile swallows every mkdir/writeFile failure (it only logs, and only when KERYX_VERBOSE is set) and resolves normally. Its only caller, runHistoryExport (line 122), then proceeds and prints 'exported N run(s) to <file>' at line 131 with exit code 0. Violates error-handling.mdc Rule 3 / Iron Law 1 (a catch that hides a failure from a caller who then proceeds). Trigger: `keryx wiki history --runs --export /readonly-dir/runs.csv` (or a target whose parent is a file).
impact: The user (or a flow/script relying on exit status) is told the export succeeded when no file was written; the failure is invisible unless they happen to set KERYX_VERBOSE. Fix: let the error propagate, or rethrow with context and `cause`.

problem: Stale/contradicting doc comment: collectRunRows claims it 'Returns the runs oldest first', but it returns listWikiRuns' order filtered, and listWikiRuns is documented and implemented as newest first (src/wiki/history.ts:495, sort at :508). Nothing reverses the array.
impact: The next reader (and any caller of this exported function) is told the wrong ordering contract; either the comment or the code must change, and the comment currently hides that the exported file is newest first.

problem: Rethrow drops the original error (no `{ cause: error }`, the bound `error` is unused) and the message names no input (which cwd / runs-log path). Violates error-handling.mdc Rules 2 and 5 / Iron Law 3.
impact: Whoever debugs a failed export loses the real reason (ENOENT, EACCES, parse) and the stack; only a generic message survives.

problem: The command-label normalisation chain (collapse newlines, collapse whitespace, trim, slice to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH) is copy-pasted three times in this change: wiki-history-export.ts:49-53 (markdown branch), wiki-history-export.ts:56-60 (CSV branch), and wiki-history.ts:47-51 (terminal listing). MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH was even exported just so the third copy could repeat it instead of sharing a helper.
impact: Any change to how labels are clipped or cleaned must be made in three places in two files and kept in sync; the doc on MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH ('in every rendered row') depends on that staying true by hand.

problem: renderRunLine takes a boolean flag `markdown` that selects between two entirely different renderers (markdown row vs CSV row), and four positional parameters where two are redundant with `run` (the only caller passes `run.pages` as `pages` and a reformatted `run.at` as `at`). Call site reads `renderRunLine(run, at, run.pages, format === "md")`.
impact: Readers must open the signature to decode the call; the timestamp formatting lives in the caller while label formatting lives in the callee, so row formatting is split across two levels. Two functions (renderCsvRow/renderMarkdownRow) taking the run, or a format-keyed renderer map, would remove the flag and the redundant arguments.
